name: Rack cases
note:
Two kinds of entry. GENERIC shells (generic: true) are how a rack arrives from a lighting rental vendor — a height in RU and nothing else — and they assert no depth, weight or payload on purpose. Identified cases carry manufacturer figures.

The case a rack actually lives in. railToRailIn is the ONLY field the depth check reads, and it is null wherever the manufacturer publishes a lid-inclusive figure instead — Gator defines its 'Rackable Depth' as Front Rail to Inside of Rear Lid, which is larger than the usable span, and Santosom publish outside dimensions only. A null runs no check; a too-generous number passes gear that will not fit. depthLabel carries the source's own words so the difference stays visible. SKB is the only manufacturer in the survey that publishes a payload FLOOR as well as a ceiling (40-150 lb standard, 160-300 lb on the factory-fitted 3SKB-SA option, uniform across case sizes) — a shock rack below its band does not isolate. Everyone else publishes a maximum or nothing. 10-32 tapped is the only touring rail thread with direct manufacturer citations (ProX, Gator, Middle Atlantic SRSR); cage nut is an install-rack convention, not a touring one.

schema.ctPid: Christie Lites product ID, where this is a CT stock item
schema.depthLabel: what the source called its depth figure, verbatim
schema.generic: true for a vendor shell known only by its RU height
schema.lidInclusiveDepthIn: a lid-inclusive figure where that is all the maker publishes
schema.railToRailIn: usable depth, rail to rail — the fit limit
